items.title: A symmetric algebra is smooth exactly when the module is finite projective
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises smoothness of the symmetric algebra of a module by finite projectivity of that module, and the proof is a 20-line argument using the cotangent complex. One direction identifies the module with the quotient of the augmentation ideal by its square and applies the criterion that a smooth algebra over a ring has finite projective conormal module; the other direction chooses a surjection onto a finite projective module, uses projectivity to split it and hence to make the symmetric algebra finitely presented, and then applies the cotangent computation of the same section to show that the naive cotangent complex is concentrated in degree zero, which is smoothness. Both directions are carried out in the source and the cotangent computation is the pivot.
